text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Macedonian government will reduce taxes by 30% for small and medium firms as part of a major project for the support and development of private initative.

- Contrary to the free trade agreement Yugoslav authorities do not issue permits for transport of goods on Yugoslav territory, which complicates trade and communication between Yugoslavia and Macedonia.
- Greece and Macedonia will negotiate at least six years before they reach a satisfactory solution to their dispute over Macedonia's name, mainly because Greece is not willing to hasten its pace.

- The Macedonian government can no longer postpone the denationalisation of private property under the pressure of the World Bank and other international financial institutions which condition their financial support and new credits with the return of property to its owners.
